intro: IEC 103 is the serial protocol of protection relays: devices that watch a power line and open its breaker when something goes wrong. A bay controller (the computer for one section, or bay, of a substation) or a gateway polls each relay in turn, on an RS-485 serial cable or an optical fiber. The relay only answers. Each signal is named by two numbers: a function type (FUN) and an information number (INF). Events carry the relay's own time.
plain: IEC 103 lets the safety devices that guard power lines report to the substation's computer. These devices, called protection relays, make a breaker switch a line off when something goes wrong, like the breakers in a home's fuse box. The computer calls on each relay in turn, like a roll call, and a relay only speaks when asked. If it has news, such as a line it just switched off, it says so in its answer, and the computer asks for the details at once.

reset.title: Reset communication
reset.text: The bay controller is the primary station: it speaks first, and the relay only answers. It starts by resetting the relay's communication unit, the part that handles the line. The relay confirms. In its reply, the ACD bit (access demand) is 1: "I have urgent data", called class 1 data.

ident.title: Who are you?
ident.text: The controller asks for class 1 data. The relay answers with its identification: manufacturer, compatibility level (which part of the standard it follows) and software version.

gi.title: Ask for everything
gi.text: The controller sends a general interrogation (GI): a request for the state of every signal. The relay confirms. The answers will come as class 1 data.

gidata.title: States arrive
gidata.text: The controller sends one class 1 request for each answer. In each new request the FCB (frame count bit) flips between 0 and 1, so the relay can tell a new request from a repeat. The last answer, type 8, says the interrogation is complete.

fault.title: Short circuit
fault.text: When nothing urgent is waiting, the controller asks for class 2 data: measurands, the measured values such as current and voltage. Then a short circuit hits the feeder, the line this relay protects. The relay trips its breaker: the breaker opens and cuts the current. But the relay cannot speak first. Its next class 2 answer shows 0 A, and ACD = 1.

trip.title: Fetch the event
trip.text: ACD = 1, so the controller asks for class 1 data at once. The trip arrives with the relay's own time, the fault number and the time since the fault began.

frames.ident: I am made by EXAMPLE, software V2.1
frames.measurands: Currents 0 A, voltages normal, 50.01 Hz. And I have an event

start-fixed.name: Start
start-fixed.note: 0x10: a fixed-length frame, 5 bytes in all.

link.name: Link address 12
link.note: 0x0C: which relay on the line. Only relay 12 answers.

cs-fixed.name: Checksum
cs-fixed.note: The control byte (C) plus the address byte (A), modulo 256. The relay checks it to spot a damaged frame.

cs-var.name: Checksum
cs-var.note: The sum of every byte from the control byte (C) to the last data byte, modulo 256.

head-21.name: Start · length
head-21.note: 68 L L 68: start, the length twice, start again. L = 0x15 = 21 bytes, from the control byte (C) to the last data byte.

head-9.name: Start · length
head-9.note: L = 9 bytes, from C to the last data byte.

c-reset.name: Control 0x40
c-reset.note: PRM 1: from the primary station. FCV 0: no frame count. Function 0: reset of the communication unit.

c-ack-acd.name: Control 0x20
c-ack-acd.note: PRM 0 (from the relay), ACD 1, function 0: ACK, "got it". ACD = 1 says the relay has class 1 data waiting: the controller should ask for it next.

c-class1-fcb1.name: Control 0x7A
c-class1-fcb1.note: PRM 1, FCB 1, FCV 1 (FCB counts), function 10: request class 1 data.

c-class1-fcb0.name: Control 0x5A
c-class1-fcb0.note: The same request with FCB 0: FCB flips with every new request.

c-class2-fcb1.name: Control 0x7B
c-class2-fcb1.note: PRM 1, FCB 1, FCV 1, function 11: request class 2 data.

c-send-fcb0.name: Control 0x53
c-send-fcb0.note: PRM 1, FCB 0, FCV 1, function 3: user data that the relay must confirm.

c-data.name: Control 0x08
c-data.note: PRM 0, ACD 0, function 8: user data. No more class 1 data.

c-data-acd.name: Control 0x28
c-data-acd.note: Function 8, user data, with ACD 1: more class 1 data is waiting.

type5.name: Type 5
type5.note: Identification: who made the relay and which software it runs.

type1.name: Type 1
type1.note: A time-tagged message: a state, with the time it was set.

type2.name: Type 2
type2.note: A time-tagged message with relative time, used for fault indications.

cot4.name: COT 4
cot4.note: Reset of the communication unit: the reason for this message.

cot9.name: COT 9
cot9.note: Sent because of the general interrogation.

cot2.name: COT 2
cot2.note: Cyclic: measured values, sent again and again as class 2 data.

ca.name: Common address
ca.note: 12 (0x0C): the relay's ASDU address, the same as its link address here.

fun160.name: FUN 160
fun160.note: 0xA0: the function type of overcurrent protection.

fun255.name: FUN 255
fun255.note: Global: for every function of the relay.

inf3.name: INF 3
inf3.note: In an identification: sent because the communication unit was reset.

inf0.name: INF 0
inf0.note: The interrogation itself, not one signal.

inf148.name: INF 148
inf148.note: 0x94: currents IL1, IL2, IL3, voltages VL1, VL2, VL3, active power P, reactive power Q and frequency f, 2 bytes each.

col2.name: Compatibility level 2
col2.note: Follows this standard's fixed message types, without the optional generic services.

software.name: Software
software.note: 4 bytes the manufacturer fills: "V2.1" in ASCII here.

scn.name: Scan number 33
scn.note: 0x21: the controller picks this number, and every answer carries it back, so it can be matched to this interrogation.

scn-end.name: Scan number 33
scn-end.note: The same number as in the command: this interrogation is complete.

dpi-on.name: DPI 2
dpi-on.note: Double-point information 2 = ON: protection is in service. 1 would be OFF.

time-gi.name: CP32Time2a
time-gi.note: A 4-byte time stamp. 0x2E10 = 11792 ms: 11.792 s, 40 min (0x28), 10 h (0x0A). Every type 1 message has a time, even in a GI answer.

time-trip.name: CP32Time2a
time-trip.note: 0x1C73 = 7283 ms: 7.283 s, 41 min, 10 h. No date, no time zone.

sin-scn.name: SIN
sin-scn.note: Supplementary information. In a GI answer, it holds the scan number of the interrogation: 33.

sin-0.name: SIN
sin-0.note: Supplementary information: 0, not used in a spontaneous message.

ret.name: Relative time
ret.note: 0x002B = 43 ms from the start of the fault to the trip.

fan.name: Fault number 18
fan.note: 0x0012: each fault gets the next number. It ties the fault's messages together.

currents.name: IL1 · IL2 · IL3
currents.note: The three phase currents: 0 A, because the breaker is open.

voltages.name: VL1 · VL2 · VL3
voltages.note: Each value is 2 bytes, low byte first. The 3 lowest bits are flags, so the value is shifted right by 3: 0x3570 >> 3 = 1710, then 1703 and 1708. 4096 means 2.4 × rated, so these are 1.002, 0.998 and 1.001 × rated: normal.

a-prm1.name: PRM
a-prm1.note: Primary message. 1: sent by the primary station, the controller.

a-fcb.name: FCB
a-fcb.note: Frame count bit: flips with every new request. The same FCB again asks for the last answer again.

a-fcv.name: FCV
a-fcv.note: Frame count valid. 1: the FCB counts in this request.

a-prm0.name: PRM
a-prm0.note: 0: sent by the secondary station, the relay.

a-acd.name: ACD
a-acd.note: Access demand: 1 means the relay has class 1 data.

a-dfc.name: DFC
a-dfc.note: Data flow control: 1 would mean the relay cannot take more data now.

facts.standard: IEC 60870-5-103 (1997), with the FT 1.2 frames of IEC 60870-5-1 and -2
facts.between: Protection relay (secondary station) → bay controller, RTU or gateway (primary)
facts.transport: RS-485 or optical fiber, 9600 or 19200 bit/s, 8 data bits and even parity
facts.security: None. Keep the line inside the substation.
facts.frames: Fixed: 10 C A CS 16 · variable: 68 L L 68 C A ASDU CS 16

tips: Only the compatible range of FUN and INF numbers is fixed by the standard. Private numbers differ between vendors, and even between firmware versions. Work from the relay's own point list.
FCB must flip with every new request. If it does not, the relay thinks its last answer was lost and sends it again.
The relay never speaks first. If the controller does not ask for class 1 when ACD = 1, events wait in the relay's buffer, and a full buffer loses them.
Time tags have no date and no time zone. Synchronize every relay (type 6 or IRIG-B) and agree on UTC or local time.

playground.file: The relay's point list, made up for this lesson. The controller needs the same list, or it cannot tell what an INF means.
playground.link: The link address: the relay's place on the line, in every frame.
playground.common: The ASDU address. Often the same as the link address.
playground.baud: Both ends must use the same speed: 9600 or 19200 bit/s.
playground.fun: FUN 160, overcurrent protection. The INF numbers below belong to it.
playground.scale: 4096 means 2.4 times the rated value. Some relays use 1.2: the controller must know which.
playground.gi: A status: sent in every general interrogation.
playground.trip: A fault indication: type 2, with relative time and fault number. Not part of the GI.
